Character limits enforced by brand.test.ts against brand.json `storeLimits`, measured with every reference resolved.
'Baby Tracker' is never the title, the subtitle or the positioning line (brand.json `banned`).

Nothing CuddleCue has and NibbleCue does not: no Community, no coins or NFC accessory, no widgets, no welcome trial.

URLs, addresses and the proposed lines are references (`brand:<key>`, or the key in double braces inside a longer text) resolved from brand.json by the accessor, never copies. A pending or unconfirmed key cannot be referenced. A PROPOSED key can, because a development build runs on it, and every proposed key this file references is listed in `waitingOnOwner`; brand.test.ts holds that list to the references.

A URL a store field needs INSIDE its text is written as its key in double braces there, like `{{termsUrl}}` (the App Store description's Terms of Use and Privacy Policy lines, which Apple 3.1.2 wants in the description or the EULA field), and is resolved by the same accessor with the same rule.

appStore.name: NibbleCue - Baby Food Planner
appStore.subtitle: brand:appleSubtitle
appStore.promotionalText: Today’s meals planned for your baby, the allergens brought in one at a time, and one log shared with CuddleCue. The free plan is a real app, with no ads.
appStore.description:
NibbleCue plans your baby’s first foods, from the first bite to toddler meals. Open it to see today’s meals, tap Served and say how it went, and the plan moves on with your baby.

{{marketingHeadline}}

What it does
· Today’s meals, each food with how to serve it at your baby’s age.
· Log a meal in two taps: Served, then how it went.
· A 14-day meal plan that follows what you log.
· A food library that shows how to serve each food at each age.
· An allergen tracker: bring in one allergen at a time, then keep each one in the week.
· Something you noticed: write down what you saw after a meal, in your own words. The emergency card is one tap away.
· A shopping list the whole household shares.
· Works with CuddleCue: the same account, the same household and the same log. A meal logged in either app is logged once.

What it does not do
NibbleCue never diagnoses and never gives a dose. A sign you write down stays something you noticed, a possible reaction to show your pediatrician, never a verdict. Serving guidance is general guidance from published sources, not medical advice. The judgment stays with you and your pediatrician.

Meal ideas, if you want more
Ask for more ideas and an AI model suggests foods for variety. It is sent a summary of foods and counts, never a name. Every idea is checked by the same safety rules as the rest of the plan, and an idea that fails a rule is never shown.

The free plan is a real app
Today’s and tomorrow’s meals, logging, the whole food library, the allergen tracker, something you noticed and the emergency card, the shopping list, light and dark, a download of everything you logged and account deletion. Safety is never sold. No ads, on any plan, and we do not sell your data.

NibbleCue Plus
The full 14-day meal plan. A caregiver sheet for whoever feeds your baby today. A pediatrician summary to bring to a visit. Milk and drinks beside the meals, read from your CuddleCue log. NibbleCue Plus is its own subscription, separate from CuddleCue Plus.

Made by the family behind CuddleCue
Dad develops, Mom designs, and the baby approves. Plus pays for the servers, the replies when you write and what we build next, so the free plan can stay a real app.

NibbleCue Plus is an auto-renewing subscription. The price is shown in the app before you buy. It renews automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the end of the period, and you can manage or cancel it in your App Store account settings. Canceling keeps NibbleCue Plus until the end of the period you paid for.

Terms of Use (EULA): {{termsUrl}}
Privacy Policy: {{privacyPolicyUrl}}
